text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A vessel carrying 40 million litres of fuel arrived in Nigeria's commercial capital Lagos on Thursday night, raising the stock imported to beat a fuel scarcity to 80 million litres.
- Erosion of the coastline along the Marina business district of Lagos has caused flooding in some parts of the city.
- The Petroleum Trust Fund has abolished its offices in Nigeria's 36 states, replacing them with a structure of six zones. The fund's chairman said the change would cut costs and improve efficiency.
- A request by Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) to increase its crude oil allocation for refineries, to 300,000 bpd from 250,000 bpd, has been turned down by the government.
- Britain may block Nigeria's return to the Commonwealth, saying it has not made big enough steps towards democratic reforms and improved human rights.
- Head of State General Sani Abacha says 7.0 billion naira has been spent over the past two years to develop Nigeria's railways.
- Importation of 33 cargoes of petroleum products, to ease a severe shortage, may cost Nigeria as much as $198 million.

- Makers of aluminium products may take raw materials from outside Nigeria even after the ALSCON Ikot Abasi smelter begins operation later this year. Companies say they have not yet been able to negotiate commercial terms with ALSCON.
